stories.headline: Global bond sell-off lifts 10-year Treasury yield to 2002 high
stories.dek: Government borrowing costs rose across major economies as investors sold bonds and pushed long-term yields to multiyear highs.
paragraphs: A broad sell-off in government bonds pushed the US 10-year Treasury yield to its highest level since 2002. Yields also climbed in other big markets. Investors have been demanding higher returns as they absorb heavy government borrowing, stubborn inflation risks and fewer expectations of fast rate cuts.

Bond yields rise when bond prices fall. The 10-year Treasury is a benchmark for borrowing across the economy, including mortgages, business loans and other debt. When its yield climbs, financing gets more expensive. Similar moves in Britain, Japan and Europe show this is not only a US market shift.

It is not yet clear whether yields will keep rising or settle at a new plateau. Much depends on inflation data, central bank signals and how much new debt governments issue. Markets are also watching whether higher yields start to slow growth, unsettle stocks or strain weaker borrowers.
stories.changes: Borrowing may stay expensive for longer, especially for mortgages, business loans and new government debt.
stories.unchanged: This does not mean an immediate financial crisis or that existing fixed-rate loans change overnight.

cover.title: US 10-year Treasury yield reaches highest level since 2002
cover.standfirst: A global bond sell-off lifted government borrowing costs in the United States and other major economies. The US 10-year Treasury yield hit its highest level in more than two decades as investors reacted to heavy debt supply, inflation risks and slower hopes for rate cuts.

art.label: Drawn chart
art.concept: A single thick, hand-drawn yield stroke runs from lower left to upper right across an otherwise empty field, reading first as a chart line and then unmistakably as a cracked whip. At the upper-right tip, the final spike lashes downward into a tiny, simplified suburban house near the bottom edge, catching the instant of impact; keep the lower third almost entirely clear apart from the house so cover lines can sit across it. No extra chart furniture, no axes, no labels — just the rising stroke, the crack, and the house.
art.note: Sober and precise; muted blues, black and a small warning red accent.
art.second_beat: First you see a yield line surging; a beat later you realise it is a whip, and that higher Treasury yields are physically striking housing and borrowing costs.

stories.headline: Russian drone strike hits grounds of Kyiv research reactor site
stories.dek: Ukraine said a fire broke out at the institute after the attack, but the VVR-M research reactor and safety systems were not damaged.
paragraphs: Ukraine said Russian drones struck the grounds of a nuclear research institute in Kyiv, raising fresh concern about attacks near nuclear sites. The state nuclear regulator said the VVR-M research reactor was not hit, safety-critical systems were not damaged, and a fire caused by the strike was quickly put out.

The site houses a research reactor, not a large power station that feeds the grid. Research reactors are used for scientific work, training and testing. Even so, any military strike on or near a nuclear facility carries special risk because damage to buildings, power supply or safety equipment can cause a wider emergency.

It is still unclear exactly where the drones landed on the institute grounds, how much non-nuclear damage was done, and whether operations at the site will be disrupted. Ukraine reported no casualties. There was no immediate independent account of the strike or a fuller public damage assessment.
stories.changes: For ordinary readers, this means another part of civilian scientific infrastructure in Kyiv is now exposed to drone attack risk.
stories.unchanged: It does not mean Kyiv suffered a reactor accident or that radiation was reported from the site.

cover.title: Russian drones strike grounds of Kyiv nuclear research institute
cover.standfirst: Ukraine said Russian drones hit the grounds of a Kyiv nuclear research institute on Friday. Officials said the VVR-M research reactor and safety systems were not damaged, a fire was quickly extinguished, and no casualties were reported. A fuller damage assessment is still pending.

art.label: Silkscreen
art.concept: A single black descending drone is staged vertically over a stark, unmistakable reactor top view: a circular core with a few severe concentric rings and simple radial geometry, read immediately as a research reactor rather than a generic target. The drone’s body is drawn so it is also a control rod being driven down into the core, caught a split second before contact; from the near-impact point, one hard red alarm halo radiates, with a second red pass slipped slightly off-register to make the warning feel unstable. Keep the lower third largely empty for type, and strip away all site clutter, buildings, and extra effects so the whole cover is just the forced downward gesture into the reactor.
art.note: Grave, restrained, black-red-grey palette with one hard emergency glow.
art.second_beat: First you see a drone strike aimed at a reactor; a beat later you realize the weapon has become a control rod, turning the attack into a grotesque emergency shutdown gesture.

stories.headline: Russia hits Ukraine power grid as winter power cuts begin
stories.dek: Seven people were killed and emergency outages were imposed in Kyiv and three regions after one of the largest energy attacks in months.
paragraphs: Russia launched a large strike on Ukraine's energy system on Wednesday, hitting facilities in Kyiv and other cities and causing emergency power cuts. The attack came as temperatures begin to fall and Ukraine enters another winter with limited air defenses and a grid already damaged by months of bombardment.

Ukraine has spent much of the war trying to keep electricity, heat and water running while Russia targets power plants, substations and other energy sites. Officials have warned for weeks that Moscow was likely to renew large attacks before winter, when blackouts can quickly turn into a public health and heating crisis.

It is not yet clear how much generating and transmission capacity was lost, how long the outages will last, or whether this was the start of a sustained winter campaign. Ukraine has threatened to answer with strikes on Russian energy assets if no truce on energy attacks is reached.
stories.changes: People in Ukraine now face a higher risk of blackouts, heating problems and service disruptions as colder weather arrives.
stories.unchanged: This does not mean Ukraine's grid has collapsed or that a formal energy truce ever existed.

cover.title: Russia strikes Ukraine power grid and forces winter blackouts
cover.standfirst: Russia launched a large attack on Ukraine's energy system on Wednesday, killing seven people and triggering emergency power cuts in Kyiv and three other regions. The strikes hit as night temperatures fall, raising the risk of a hard winter if more attacks follow.

art.label: Engraving
art.concept: Inside a Kyiv apartment-block stairwell during a blackout, show a single resident in a heavy winter coat and gloves descending the stairs with a metal bucket of water. Behind them, the lift stands dead and open as a black rectangle; the stairwell is almost entirely dark except for a thin wedge of light from one apartment door high above, with banisters and steps dropping away into engraved black. Keep the lower third mostly quiet: just the descending steps, the bucket, and darkness.
art.note: Silent, severe, cold blue-grey palette with small warm points of light.
art.second_beat: First you see a blackout stairwell; a beat later the bucket, dead lift and winter clothing make clear that power, water and heat have all failed together.

stories.headline: Micron sues YMTC over engineers and disputed memory patents
stories.dek: Micron says former staff took 3D NAND know-how to YMTC, then became inventors on patents now used against Micron in court.
paragraphs: Micron has sued Chinese memory maker YMTC, accusing it of hiring away Micron engineers, taking confidential 3D NAND knowledge, and turning that knowledge into products and patents. The case matters now because Micron says YMTC is already using some of those patents to sue Micron in other courts.

3D NAND is the flash memory used in phones, PCs, and data centers. Big memory companies often avoid direct patent wars through cross-licensing deals. Micron says YMTC, a newer Chinese rival, built part of its patent portfolio through former Micron staff who had access to sensitive process and design information.

Micron still has to prove that trade secrets were taken, that YMTC used them, and that the patents should not be enforced against Micron. Patent records show some former Micron engineers later appeared as inventors on YMTC patents, but courts will decide whether that amounts to theft or ordinary employee movement.
stories.changes: It could deepen the legal fight behind the chips that end up in everyday electronics and cloud services.
stories.unchanged: This does not mean memory supplies or consumer device prices will change right away.

cover.title: Micron says YMTC used ex-staff to build patents
cover.standfirst: Micron has filed a lawsuit in Idaho accusing Chinese memory maker YMTC of hiring its engineers, taking confidential 3D NAND know-how, and using it to build products and patent claims. Micron says some of those patents were later used to sue Micron in California and other courts.

art.label: Punk cutout
art.concept: On an acid-green ground, stage a single cleanroom bunny-suit figure twice across the upper half only: at left, stepping out through a fab doorway marked only by Micron’s unmistakable memory-chip silhouette language; at right, the same figure stepping into a contrasting YMTC fab doorway. Between the two moments, black stepped 3D-NAND layer strips are visibly slipping from a slit in the suit and trailing with the body like contraband, so the transfer of invisible process know-how becomes physical; keep the lower third empty and kill every extra detail except doors, figure, and the stolen layers.
art.note: Sharp, accusatory collage in cold gray, black, and acid red.
art.second_beat: First you see one worker moving from one fab to another; a beat later you realize the thing being carried is not objects but Micron’s 3D-NAND know-how, now arriving inside YMTC.

stories.headline: Family rescued from floodwater as heavy rain hits Melbourne
stories.dek: Police pulled four people from two stranded cars under a South Melbourne bridge after parts of the city got about 35 millimetres of rain.
paragraphs: A couple and their two children were rescued on Thursday after their car became trapped in rising water under the York Street bridge in South Melbourne. Police also rescued people from a second car nearby. Heavy rain swept across Melbourne, and authorities expect more falls into Friday and Saturday.

Emergency services received more than 120 calls for help on Thursday afternoon, with many from Malvern and Port Phillip. Several parts of Melbourne recorded about 35 millimetres of rain, close to half the city’s average October rainfall in one day. Another truck and van became stuck in floodwater at Elwood.

Victoria is now on flood watch across 18 river catchments in the state’s north-east, Gippsland and central regions. The SES says minor to moderate flooding is possible from Friday into the weekend and has told residents not to drive through floodwater. The full extent of flooding will depend on rain still to come overnight.
stories.changes: People in Melbourne and parts of Victoria may face road closures, transport delays and fast-changing local flood risks through the weekend.
stories.unchanged: This does not mean all of Melbourne is flooding, and no injuries were reported in these rescues.

cover.title: Police rescue family from cars trapped in Melbourne floodwater
cover.standfirst: A family of four and other motorists were rescued after two cars became stuck under the York Street bridge in South Melbourne on Thursday afternoon. More than 120 calls for help were made as about 35 millimetres of rain fell across parts of the city, with more rain and possible river flooding forecast into the weekend.

art.label: Gouache painting
art.concept: Paint the York Street bridge underpass in South Melbourne front-on, unmistakably as that low road tunnel, with muddy floodwater risen almost to the lip so the whole opening reads as an overfilled bathtub made from ordinary city infrastructure. Inside the pooled water, two real cars sit trapped and skewed at different depths — one nearer, with a family being pulled up and out by Victoria Police from the dry roadway edge above, the second farther back only partly visible, nosed into the murk. Keep the lower third a broad, flat brown water mass for type; let the action and police lights sit around the rim, so the horror is that this banal underpass has become a container holding people and cars.
art.note: Cold, rain-heavy mood; slate grey, muddy brown and washed blue palette.
art.second_beat: First you see a road tunnel turned impossibly into a tub; then you register that the tiny floating cars contain a family being lifted out, making the scale suddenly frightening.

stories.headline: Swiss glaciers lose 5.5% of ice volume in one year
stories.dek: Heat waves and weak winter snowfall drove one of the steepest annual losses ever measured across Switzerland's glaciers.
paragraphs: Swiss glacier experts said the country’s glaciers lost 5.5% of their total ice volume in 2026, the second-largest yearly drop on record. They blamed repeated heat waves and low winter snowfall, which left less snow to shield older ice and less fresh snow to turn into new glacier ice.

Switzerland holds the most glaciers in the Alps. Scientists say nearly a fifth of the country’s glacier volume has disappeared in the past five years alone. From July to September, meltwater loss reached 2.2 trillion liters. That is about four times Switzerland’s yearly water use and affects rivers fed from the Alps.

The immediate question is how much more ice can survive repeated hot summers before some glaciers break apart or vanish. Scientists say cutting carbon emissions can still limit future losses, especially in polar ice sheets, but they also warn it may already be too late to save many glaciers in the Swiss Alps.
stories.changes: It means faster glacier loss is no longer a distant trend and will affect water, landscapes and hydropower across the Alps.
stories.unchanged: It does not mean Switzerland is suddenly running out of drinking water this year or that every Alpine glacier will disappear at once.

cover.title: Swiss glaciers lost 5.5% of their ice this year
cover.standfirst: Swiss scientists say heat waves and low winter snow cut the country’s glacier volume by 5.5% in 2026, one of the worst annual losses on record. Some glaciers thinned by up to four meters on average, and experts say many in the Swiss Alps may no longer survive in the long term.

art.label: Decorative flat
art.concept: A Swiss Alpine valley seen obliquely in decorative flat shapes: dark patterned ridges on both sides, and between them a single broad glacier tongue that is also the exact form of a braided meltwater system. Up-valley it reads as solid white ice; halfway down it splits into narrow stream-ribbons and pours downhill as if the glacier itself is turning into runoff in real time. Keep the lower third mostly quiet with a few clean channels crossing open darker ground, and place one tiny hiker on a marked mountain path at the side for scale.
art.note: Clear, unsentimental, cool blues and whites against raw rock brown.
art.second_beat: First you see a glacier; a beat later you realize the glacier has become the river replacing it, with the tiny hiker making that transformation feel immediate and real.

stories.headline: US leaves key NATO allies out of Poland strategy meeting
stories.dek: Britain, France and the Baltic states were not invited to an October Pentagon-led group session on NATO's future.
paragraphs: The Trump administration has left several major NATO allies out of an October meeting in Poland on the alliance's future, according to diplomats cited by Politico. The Pentagon-led session comes as Washington builds a smaller working group of countries it says are meeting defense goals and ready for practical planning.

The invited countries are Norway, Sweden, Finland, Poland, Germany and the Netherlands. The format, known as the Bergen Group, has already met twice under US defense policy chief Elbridge Colby. Britain, France, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania were excluded, despite their central role in European defense and in deterring Russia.

It is still unclear how Washington chose the group, whether more countries will be added, and how much influence its proposals will carry inside NATO. US officials have not publicly explained the exclusions. Diplomats fear the process could split allies into favored and disfavored camps at a sensitive moment for Europe.

cover.title: US leaves key NATO allies out of Poland strategy meeting
cover.standfirst: Britain, France and the Baltic states were not invited to an October Pentagon-led group session on NATO's future.

art.label: Object photograph
art.concept: On a clean NATO-blue paper sweep, place a single clear drinking glass slightly above centre, leaving the lower third empty for type. Inside the glass, only seven miniature desk flags on identical chrome stands are tightly contained and upright: the US, Poland, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and Finland. Just outside the glass, five matching flags are unmistakably excluded and in motion — Britain, France, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania tipped on their sides at the rim or sliding away from it, as if they have just failed to make it in; keep everything else out of frame so the image is only the vessel, the invited cluster and the rejected frontline allies.
art.second_beat: First it reads as flags trapped in a glass; a beat later you realise the ones left outside are precisely the allies you would most expect to be included.

stories.headline: France arrests more than 600 as school protests turn violent
stories.dek: Student blockades over class conditions spread to 356 schools, with fires, tear gas and injuries in Paris, Lyon, Bordeaux and Lille.
paragraphs: French police detained more than 600 people on Wednesday as student protests at high schools spread and turned more violent. Officials said 356 schools were affected. The government says some demonstrations now include arson, thrown objects and attacks on police, teachers and school property.

The protests began last week in the Paris region and spread across France. Students say classes are overcrowded, workloads are too heavy, materials are poor and too few teachers are available. Some also describe dirty, badly heated school buildings. Blockades at lycees have become the main form of protest.

It is still unclear whether the protests will grow or fade after the mass arrests. President Emmanuel Macron said students' complaints are legitimate but violence is not. The government blames far-left agitators for worsening clashes, while left-wing opponents accuse officials of using an excessive crackdown.
stories.changes: Students, parents and teachers in France may face more police presence, school closures and disruption if blockades continue.
stories.unchanged: This does not mean France's whole school system has shut down or that every student protest has turned violent.

cover.title: France arrests hundreds as high school protests spread
cover.standfirst: French police detained more than 600 people on Wednesday after student protests hit 356 schools. Teenagers are protesting overcrowded classes, teacher shortages and poor building conditions. Clashes in Paris, Lyon, Bordeaux and Lille left police, teachers and pupils injured, and the government now faces pressure to restore order without deepening anger.

art.label: Made object
art.concept: Build a single handmade French lycée facade from card and felt, seen straight-on against one flat bright ground, with its entrance unmistakably blocked by a jammed barricade made only of school things: a chair, ruler, backpack, exercise books and a desk edge wedged across the doors. From inside that pile, one bright felt flame is just catching and two or three clay marbles are mid-flight outward, so the scene is at the instant a school blockade tips into violence; keep glue strings, fingerprints and rough craft edges visible, and leave the lower third mostly clear except for the base of the barricade.
art.note: Tense and public; muted reds, navy, grey and dirty cream.
art.second_beat: First you see a school protest blockade; then you realise the objects of education themselves have become both the barricade and the weapons as it turns violent.

stories.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Argon for coding and cyber defense
stories.dek: The new AI model is being given first to selected security partners, with Google saying it can find and patch serious software flaws.
paragraphs: Google has released Gemini 4 Argon, its newest artificial intelligence model, and says it is its strongest system so far. The company is pitching it for coding, research, writing and especially defensive cybersecurity work. For now, Google is giving access only to selected cyber partners through its Fairwind Program.

Argon is part of the fast competition among major AI companies to ship larger and more capable models. Google says Argon can analyze images, charts and long videos, and can help with debugging and moving old code into new systems. It also claims the model outperforms recent systems from OpenAI and Anthropic on several benchmarks.

It is still not clear how well Argon will perform outside Google's own tests and chosen benchmarks. Google has not opened it to the public, so independent users cannot yet judge its reliability or safety in real security work. The wider question of how much autonomy AI tools should have in sensitive systems also remains unsettled.

cover.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Argon for coding and cyber defense
cover.standfirst: The new AI model is being given first to selected security partners, with Google saying it can find and patch serious software flaws.

art.label: Maximalist doodle
art.concept: A diagonal intake line of software bugs — beetles, moths, centipedes and aphids with tiny circuit-board traces on their shells — snakes in from the upper left toward a Google-like data-centre security gate in the upper half of the cover. At the gate, scanner arms and mechanical patch tools are actively grabbing the bugs one by one, cracking them open and converting them into neat repaired metal components that exit the other side, while a few waiting bugs stand calmly in queue as if this were a routine partner-only checkpoint; keep the lower third largely clear white for type, with the whole scene built in dense maximalist doodle detail only above and around the queue.
art.second_beat: First you see pests at a security gate; then it clicks that the vulnerabilities are not attacking but being deliberately admitted, inspected and turned into patches — the private intake line is the story.

stories.headline: Reddit will shut RSS feeds and public API access
stories.dek: The company says scraping and bot abuse drove the change, with RSS ending first and public API access ending in March 2027.
paragraphs: Reddit said it will end support for RSS feeds and later shut down public API access. The company says both tools are now used for large-scale scraping and automated abuse. RSS feeds are due to shut on November 13, while public API access will end in March 2027.

RSS lets people and apps follow new posts in a standard feed reader. Reddit's public API lets outside developers, researchers, monitoring tools, and AI products pull Reddit conversations by software. Reddit has become more protective of that data as it builds a business selling access to its user-generated content.

Moderators who use RSS for alerts are being told to move to Reddit's Discord Relay Devvit app, but there is no replacement for general public RSS use. It is still unclear how much research, moderation, and third-party tools will be lost, and which services will pay Reddit for continued access.
stories.changes: For ordinary readers, it will be harder to follow Reddit in RSS apps or through outside tools that depend on free programmatic access.
stories.unchanged: This does not mean Reddit is disappearing or that every third-party app will stop working immediately; approved and registered tools can still operate for now.

cover.title: Reddit will close RSS feeds and public API access
cover.standfirst: Reddit says RSS feeds will shut on November 13 and public API access will end in March 2027. The company says scraping and automated abuse forced the change. Moderators are being told to move alert systems, while researchers, AI tools, and outside apps may need paid deals.

art.label: Newsprint collage
art.concept: A large pair of scissors made from torn newspaper photos and dense type is caught mid-snip through a single curling strip of feed paper, staged diagonally so the action is unmistakable. The opened gap between the blades and the severed strip forms the clear silhouette of the Reddit Snoo head — round head, one antenna nub, simple profile — so Reddit appears only as the hole created by the cut. Keep the background painted and plain, with the lower third largely empty except for the tail of the falling strip.
art.note: Clean, spare, slightly cold; white, orange, black, and muted gray.
art.second_beat: First you see a feed being cut off; a beat later you realize the cut itself makes Reddit, turning the company into the absence it creates.
